newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT-Argentine ADRs stretch gains,trade thin.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT-Argentine ADRs stretch gains,trade thin.

text.p: Argentine shares stretched their gains on thin U.S. volumes Monday, buoyed by Argentina's tentative deal with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and strength in the Dow.
Traders said the IMF's tentative agreement to issue an Extended Fund Facility loan to Argentina in September next year was viewed positively by the market, although it was widely expected.
"Argentina had a pretty good meeting over the weekend with the IMF," a trader said. "But I don't think anyone thought that the IMF would not give them the waiver."
Michel Camdessus, managing director of the IMF, met Argentine President Carlos Menem over the weekend and praised the country's plans for fiscal and labor reforms.
Traders said the market appeared to be unfazed by the resignation of Economy Ministry advisor Guillermo Calvo on Friday and the planned departure of another official.
"That really doesn't seem to bother people as long as (Economy Minister Roque) Fernandez is still there," one said.
Argentine oil giant YPF's American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) rose 1/2 to 22-3/4, while Telefonica gained 1/2 to 24-3/4 and Banco Frances added 1/2 to 24-5/8.
Troubled Pepsi bottler BAESA was one of the country's few losers, sliding 1/4 to 6-3/4 after weeks of volatile trade.

Elsewhere, Mexican shares were mixed on paltry volumes after their sharp rise Friday. "Mexico has had a very good run over the last few months, and a lot of these stocks have gotten ahead of themselves," a trader said.
Mexican blue chip Telmex was flat at 33 after Lehman cut its 1997 earnings estimate on the stock but kept its outperform rating.
Tribasa added 1/4 to 5-5/8, Televisa slid 1/4 to 30-3/8 and Tamsa was flat at 11-1/4.
Other Latin American shares were little changed, with Telebras up 5/8 at 76-1/8, CTC off 3/4 at 97-5/8, and Telefonica del Peru flat at 23-3/8.
"You're not seeing a lot of money moving into Latin American funds right now, and I don't think we'll see the next big move until we do," a trader said.
Among other ADRs, Britain's Danka soared over 16 percent on news of its alliance with Eastman Kodak and acquisition of Kodak's Office Imaging business operations.
